newsitem.title: ITALY: Gemina details H1 '96 industrial sales.
newsitem.headline: Gemina details H1 '96 industrial sales.

text.p: Italian financial holding group Gemina said it had first-half 1996 industrial sales, from its divisions which will make up its new industrial holding company, of some three trillion lire.

Gemina has said it intends to split its industrial holdings into a new holding group called Holding Partecipazioni Industriali (HPI), which will include its publishing group RCS, sports clothing Fila, paper group Burgo and other divisions.

Gemina's managing director Paolo Sabatini told an analysts meeting that these industrial groupings had operating profits in the first half of 1996 of around six percent of sales, or around 180 billion lire, and net profits at around four percent of sales, or around 120 billion lire.
At June 30, HPI shareholders equity was around four trillion lire and debt was one trillion lire.
HPI is intended to be launched before the end of the year, after a Gemina shareholders meeting on November 27, he said.
Gemina said its RCS unit saw sales up 11 percent in the first nine months of 1996.
